payload.title: Wedding Guest List Template for Google Sheets and Excel
protect_keywords: wedding guest list template google sheets
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s, 12 to 18 months out from a destination wedding with 60 to 90 guests (many flying in), who searched for a guest list template and want a proper file they can download in one click, understand every column, share safely with a parent or helper, and keep using as flights, rooms, welcome dinner replies and visa letters start to come in.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor (Wedded Concierge enquiry), reached after the reader has downloaded the template and seen how much guest travel logistics it has to carry.

payload.angle: Page one for this keyword is forum threads, sign-up-gated downloads, pin boards and old blog templates built for a local reception. Ours is a no-sign-up .xlsx we built ourselves: it opens in Excel and imports straight into Google Sheets, carries the standard columns a reader expects (household, names, contact, side, events invited, RSVP, headcount, meals, dietary, plus-ones, gifts, thank-yous) and adds the destination columns nobody else ships: arrival and departure, flights booked, accommodation, welcome dinner RSVP, and visa letter needed and sent. Then it explains every column, how to fill it in by household and by event, and how to share it with helpers without being careless with other people's details.
must_include: Intro: the no-sign-up download (button/link above the fold) plus exactly 4 one-sentence key takeaways. No 'free' in headings or takeaways.

Download and open: how to open the .xlsx in Excel, and how to import it into Google Sheets (upload then open, or File > Import). Plain steps; Google Sheets and Excel named only as file formats/apps, no other vendors.

The columns explained, core columns first, then destination columns (arrival and departure, flights booked, accommodation, welcome dinner RSVP, visa letter needed, visa letter sent), one short 'what it is for' line each. Column names must match the .xlsx exactly (writer checks against the download folder).

How to fill it in: one row per household with names per guest, side (for counting only), per-event invites (welcome dinner, ceremony, reception, recovery brunch), plus-one and children rule decided once and noted at the top of the sheet. A and B lists presented only as an optional choice, not a recommendation; no timing rules or percentages.

Destination columns in use: tracking arrivals for transfers and room blocks, who still needs flights, welcome dinner numbers separate from the wedding RSVP. Visa letters: tell readers to check the destination's official entry requirements for each guest's passport; state no country rules.

Privacy and sharing with helpers: what you are holding (addresses, dietary and health details, passport-related info), share view-only or a cut-down tab, remove passport numbers you do not need, delete or archive after the wedding. Australian privacy facts sourced from the OAIC only, labelled 'general information as at November 2026, not legal advice'.

Other formats as plain guidance (printable, Word, PDF, Canva: how to print or export from the .xlsx, or rebuild the columns in your own design tool) with no third-party template links; then when to move into Wonderland Studio, described only as 'our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs'.

FAQ (5 to 7 questions from People Also Ask / the live page's FAQ themes), then close with exactly one Wedded Advisor line built from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' (e.g. one Wedded Advisor as a single point of contact, guest room blocks held by the advisor), CTA 'Speak with a Wedded Advisor' to /wonderland-concierge with UTMs.
keep_from_live_page: Ideas only, rewritten (live wording is not to be reused): count households first then people; the envelope name column differs from how you say a name; dietary needs separate from meal choice (allergies are not preferences); record the date an invitation was sent, not a tick; decide the plus-one and children rule once and write it at the top of the sheet; an 'events invited' column because not every guest gets every event; gift received and thank-you sent columns.

avoid: Prices of any kind, 'From AUD' figures
'Best', 'free', 'ultimate' and superlatives in headings and copy
Statistics, decline rates, percentages, guest-count thresholds, week counts
Vendor, app or template-site names (Google Sheets and Excel only as file formats); no third-party template links
Country-specific visa or entry rules; any legal advice beyond OAIC general information
Wonderland Studio feature claims beyond 'our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs'
Reusing the live page's wording or any competitor wording; sample personal data that looks real
Duplicating /expert-advice/how-to-make-a-wedding-guest-list (who to invite, how to cut the list) or the RSVP guides (deadlines, wording, reminders)
Clichés (dream day, fairytale), hard-sell CTAs, em dashes, US spelling
